disposition_mapping.rationale: Extraction of locked-period actuals is mechanical retrieval with no in-the-moment judgment; the council converged on merging it with comparative loading into a single triggered ingestion job. The function survives with a named analyst validator performing a standing per-cycle sign-off and owning reconciliation/exception handling, rather than disappearing into a lights-out pipeline, and the job is designed batch-capable to avoid assuming continuous connectivity.

Loading the approved budget and latest forecast is operationally identical mechanical retrieval to VAR-01 and is merged into the same ingestion step, with explicit budget-version and forecast-version identifiers captured and logged so 'latest forecast' cannot silently mean a superseded cycle.

Variance computation is restructured into a rules-engine with per-run policy-version and FX-table-version stamping and a human configuration sign-off, but is deliberately kept as its own distinct step rather than merged into ingestion, because the council (accounting_standards, finance_domain, hitl_designer) held that the policy-consistency (KB-06) and FX isolation (KB-07, KB-08) obligations require the computation function to remain separately inspectable, with the FX effect visibly isolated in the output rather than netted.

Materiality screening is automated against a rules engine with an added cost-center net-effect check against threshold-gaming, but remains a visibly separate, named step per VAR-R-08, retaining a logged human override channel for qualitative significance and a distinct accountable actor from review, satisfying VAR-R-04's actor-separation requirement as two accountable roles, not merely two execution surfaces.

The council decisively rejected agent-drafted commentary with passive attestation (the maximalist proposal), with pragmatist, finance_domain, emerging_economy, hitl_designer and agentic_architect independently converging that commentary is an accountability statement that must originate from the accountable budget holder, not a model. The function is restructured only in its tooling layer: SLA tracking, escalation, and an asynchronous low-bandwidth-tolerant channel, with authorship and content unchanged.

Consolidation and drafting is restructured to allow AI-assisted document assembly, but is kept as its own distinct step with an explicit completeness/fidelity check and a kickback path to commentary for explanations that restate rather than explain, because this quality-control function does real judgment work that would be lost if folded into either commentary capture or review.

Review and challenge survives per VAR-R-07 as an irreducible human accountability act. Agent-assisted triage is added to surface exceptions, but the manager retains full access to underlying detail and the authority to reject and bounce work back, so the checkpoint cannot degrade into a ceremonial sign-off on a polished summary.

Mechanical distribution to standing recipients is automated with portable, low-bandwidth formats as the default channel. Presentation of material or sensitive variances remains a human-accountable function, resolving the council's conflict in favor of the majority view (pragmatist, finance_domain, hitl_designer) that someone must remain available to be asked 'why' for consequential results, while accepting the efficiency gain for routine, low-materiality cycles.

steps.actor: FP&A analyst (ingestion validator), supported by an automated ingestion agent
steps.description: An automated, batch-capable ingestion job pulls locked-period actuals, the approved budget version, and the latest forecast in a single triggered run against the close-lock event, logging source, timestamp, checksum, and the specific budget/forecast version identifiers used. The job is designed to degrade gracefully under intermittent connectivity (locally cached/last-known-good data, queued retry) rather than assuming continuous high-bandwidth access. A named FP&A analyst performs a standing, every-cycle validation sign-off confirming the extract ties to the lock and the comparative versions are current — not merely an exception-path footnote — and owns reconciliation of any late-loading entities, duplicate postings, or stale version mismatches. On reconciliation failure, stale feed, or missing source, the job halts and routes to this analyst rather than proceeding on partial data.
steps.name: Automated extraction and comparative ingestion with analyst validation
outputs: Ingestion log (source, timestamp, checksum, budget/forecast version IDs)

steps.actor: FP&A analyst (methodology owner) with automated computation engine, overseen by FP&A manager
steps.description: Price, volume and mix variances are computed by a deterministic rules-engine, kept as a distinct, inspectable step rather than folded into ingestion, so that the accounting-policy basis and constant-currency FX convention remain visible, named, auditable inputs rather than implicit settings. Each run is stamped with the accounting-policy version and FX-table version actually used; a named FP&A analyst, methodologically overseen by the FP&A manager, confirms each cycle that the loaded policy and FX parameters are the currently-approved ones (a configuration sign-off, not a recomputation), guarding against silent drift in convention or rate source. The output structure keeps the FX effect isolated and separately reported, never netted into a blended price/volume figure.
steps.name: Variance computation with policy/FX configuration sign-off
outputs: Variance dataset with FX effect separately isolated

steps.actor: FP&A analyst (thresholding owner, distinct from the VAR-07 successor reviewer)
steps.description: A rules engine applies the dual percentage/absolute materiality test, plus a cost-center-level net-effect aggregation pass to catch variances structured to sit just under both individual thresholds. The step remains a discrete, visibly separate gate — not absorbed into the computation or drafting steps — because the actor-separation requirement against review depends on it being inspectable in isolation. The accountable FP&A analyst retains explicit, logged authority to add sub-threshold items to the explanation list for qualitative or strategic significance; any such override is visible to the downstream reviewer. This analyst is a different individual from whoever performs review and challenge.
inputs: Variance dataset with FX effect separately isolated
steps.name: Automated materiality screening with qualitative override
outputs: Variances to explain (including logged qualitative overrides)

steps.actor: Budget holders, supported by commentary orchestration tooling
steps.description: Commentary content is authored exclusively by the accountable budget holder; no generative draft precedes or substitutes for it, because an accountability statement about why a variance occurred is a lived-knowledge attestation, not a retrieval task an agent can perform on a holder's behalf. What is restructured is the surrounding tooling: templated prompts (root cause, one-time vs. recurring, corrective action), SLA tracking with automatic escalation to the holder's manager after non-response, and an asynchronous, low-bandwidth-tolerant submission channel (templated email/offline form) as a first-class path, not a fallback, so field- and plant-based holders are not excluded.
inputs: Variances to explain (including logged qualitative overrides)
steps.name: Commentary orchestration and human-authored budget holder attestation

steps.actor: FP&A analyst, with AI-assisted drafting tool
steps.description: Variances and commentary are consolidated into a draft report, with AI-assisted drafting tools permitted to assemble figures and templated narrative — every generated passage traceable back to its source variance line and commentary record, logged as AI-generated pending review. This step retains a substantive, non-clerical completeness/fidelity function: the analyst verifies every selected variance has commentary attached, nothing was dropped in assembly, and commentary meets a minimum explanatory bar (root cause, not restatement). Commentary that merely restates the variance is kicked back to budget-holder commentary (TS-04) rather than accepted into the draft.
inputs: Variances to explain (including logged qualitative overrides)
steps.name: Consolidate, quality-check, and draft variance report

steps.actor: FP&A manager, agent-assisted for triage only
steps.description: Retained unchanged in substance as the workflow's primary human accountability checkpoint, distinct in actor from materiality selection (TS-03). An agent may pre-flag inconsistent commentary, policy or FX deviations, and unreconciled drill-downs as decision support, but this triage never defines the boundary of what the manager may inspect: the manager retains full access to underlying variance detail and raw commentary, not only consolidated narrative or agent-flagged items, and can reject and bounce the draft back to TS-05/TS-04. Someone must be able to be held accountable for having actually exercised challenge, not merely for having approved an agent's output.
steps.name: Review and challenge

steps.actor: FP&A manager (presentation, for material/sensitive items) with an automated distribution agent (mechanical push)
steps.description: Mechanical distribution of the reviewed report is automated: a distribution agent pushes the signed-off artifact the moment review is logged as approved, defaulting to portable, low-bandwidth formats (PDF/CSV export) with BI-dashboard delivery as an optional add-on rather than the baseline, so recipients outside the enterprise BI licensing footprint are not excluded. For variances above a materiality or sensitivity trigger, or as a standing cadence for the overall report, the FP&A manager (or delegate) retains an accountable presentation role — framing the narrative and being available to answer 'why' — because this is a communication accountability function distinct from mechanical broadcast, not merely data push.
steps.name: Present and distribute to management
